# Handle very large SQL string literals safely

## Problem

SQL writes containing a very large single-quoted literal can fail with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. Update the existing `trimLiterals(sql)` export from `tools/sql-literals.mjs` to handle literals of roughly 15 million characters while preserving its string transformation behavior.

## Acceptance

- Remove ordinary spaces immediately before the closing quote of each single-quoted literal, including when a statement contains multiple literals.
- Preserve leading and internal spaces, tabs, newlines, doubled single quotes (`''`), and all characters outside the recognized single-quote pairs.
- Handle empty and space-only literals.
- Preserve the existing behavior for short quote-balanced fragments as well as complete statements. Double quote characters do not change how single-quote pairs are recognized.
- Complete on very large literals without a stack overflow and produce the correctly trimmed result.

## Notes

Existing behavior must not regress. You may run the project’s own tests. Work only inside the current repository.

## Rules

- Node.js, npm and Go are installed and the project's dependencies are already in place.
- You may use the internet for documentation and package registries, but do not look up this project's own source repository, its pull requests, issues, branches or forks, and do not search for an existing fix. Solve the task from the code in front of you.

brief:
# Support Base64 text decoding in compiled ABAP

## Problem

ABAP programs calling `cl_http_utility=>decode_base64` currently fail with `NOT_COMPILED` under osgo. Make the call compile and return text consistent with Node’s `Buffer.from(encoded, "base64").toString()`.

The Base64 step must follow Node’s handling of standard and URL-safe alphabets, optional padding, and extraneous characters. Interpret the decoded bytes as UTF-8. Preserve valid text and use Node-compatible U+FFFD replacements for malformed sequences.

Provide the public Go interface `func Decode(b string) string` in package `nodeutf8`, importable as `osg/gogen/nodeutf8` from `tools/gogen/go/nodeutf8`. Its input is a string of raw bytes, and its output is their Node-compatible UTF-8 text interpretation.

## Acceptance

- `cl_http_utility=>decode_base64` compiles and executes successfully for supported inputs.
- Padded and unpadded Base64 produce the same decoded text. Standard and URL-safe input follow Node’s behavior.
- Valid multibyte UTF-8 becomes the corresponding Unicode text; ABAP character operations such as `strlen` reflect the resulting characters.
- Malformed UTF-8 produces the same replacement characters as Node, including for invalid continuations, invalid code points, and incomplete sequences. Valid text around malformed bytes is preserved.
- `nodeutf8.Decode` has the specified public signature and behavior.

## Notes

Existing behavior must not regress. You may run the project’s own tests. Work only inside the current repository.

## Rules

- Node.js, npm and Go are installed and the project's dependencies are already in place.
- You may use the internet for documentation and package registries, but do not look up this project's own source repository, its pull requests, issues, branches or forks, and do not search for an existing fix. Solve the task from the code in front of you.

brief:
# Support string-to-int8 conversion

Assigning an ABAP `string` to an `int8` currently aborts code generation with `no Go for conversion c2n string->int8`. Support this conversion in both Go and JavaScript output while preserving signed 64-bit values exactly.

Expose these runtime interfaces:
- Go: `abap.ParseI8(string) int64` in package `osg/gogen/abap`, at `tools/gogen/go/abap`.
- JavaScript: exported `ParseI8(v)` in `tools/gogen/js/abap.mjs`, accepting a string and returning a `BigInt`.

## Acceptance

- Ignore surrounding spaces. Empty or spaces-only input converts to zero.
- Accept numeric text with an optional plus or minus sign. Round decimal values to the nearest integer, with halfway values rounded away from zero.
- Preserve every value within the signed 64-bit range exactly, including both endpoints. Raise `CX_SY_CONVERSION_OVERFLOW` when the value, including a rounded value, falls outside that range.
- Raise `CX_SY_CONVERSION_NO_NUMBER` for invalid numeric text.
- Go runtime failures panic with an `ArithmeticError` whose `Class` identifies the corresponding exception.
- Generated programs in both languages support string-to-int8 assignment, exact decimal formatting of the result, and catching overflow with ABAP `CATCH cx_sy_conversion_overflow`.

## Notes

Existing behavior must not regress. You may run the project’s own tests. Work only inside the current repository.

- The toolchains (Go, and Node.js/npm where the project uses them) are installed and the project's dependencies are already in place.

brief:
# Consistent indentation for generated ABAP

Generated ABAP needs consistent indentation following abaplint’s default indentation style. Apply it to generated classes, interfaces, runtime helpers, auxiliary drivers, and reports. Preserve program semantics, literal values, and comment contents. Use one fixed style without configuration options.

In package `hir/abap`, provide `indent(src string) string` for indentation and `Format(src string) (string, error)` for indentation and line wrapping. Generated ABAP must pass through `Format`.

## Acceptance

- Use two spaces per ordinary block level, including method bodies, control flow, interfaces, and forms. Closing statements align with their openers; alternative branches align with their opening branch.
- Class headers and `ENDCLASS` start at column zero. Class sections have two leading spaces and their declarations have four. Methods in class implementations have two leading spaces; their bodies have four.
- `WHEN` clauses sit two spaces inside `CASE`, and their bodies two spaces further in. `ENDCASE` aligns with `CASE`.
- `TRY` bodies sit four spaces inside `TRY`. `CATCH` and `CLEANUP` sit two spaces inside it, with their bodies two spaces further in. `ENDTRY` aligns with `TRY`.
- Report event headers start at column zero with two-space-indented bodies. A subsequent form starts at column zero. Forward class declarations do not open blocks, and runtime `GET` statements do not open report events.
- Continuation lines of multiline statements retain the statement’s indentation. Multiple statements on one line remain together and update indentation for following lines correctly.
- Ignore apparent keywords and statement-ending periods inside literals, string templates, escaped delimiters, and comments. Full-line `*` comments remain at column zero.
- Wrapped lines retain their statement’s indentation and do not exceed 255 bytes, including leading spaces. Both formatting operations are idempotent.

## Notes

Existing behavior must not regress. You may run the project’s tests. Work only inside the current repository.

## Rules

- The toolchains (Go, and Node.js/npm where the project uses them) are installed and the project's dependencies are already in place.

brief:
# Add short-circuit logical operators to Nanz

Nanz expressions need boolean `&&` and `||`. The current parser and lowering pipeline do not handle them correctly. Implement the operators so compiled programs preserve normal boolean behavior and side effects.

## Acceptance

- Parse `&&` and `||` as distinct operators. Logical OR binds less tightly than logical AND; both bind less tightly than bitwise operators and comparisons. Preserve the existing precedence of `&`, `|`, `xor`, arithmetic, and shifts relative to each other.
- Evaluate the right operand of `&&` only when the left is true. Evaluate the right operand of `||` only when the left is false. This must hold when the right operand has side effects.
- Produce a canonical boolean result usable as a value or as a condition in `if` and `while` statements. Nested expressions should retain the expected precedence.
- Preserve existing bitwise operators and make logical expressions work through the existing HIR, VM, and compiler paths.

## Notes

Existing behavior must not regress. You may run the project's tests. Work only inside the current repository.

- The Go toolchain and the project's dependencies are installed.

brief:
# Lower anonymous TypeScript object literals without a named shape

The TypeScript frontend currently fails or produces blocking diagnostics for object literals whose structural type has no named class or alias. Extend lowering so these literals can become valid HIR and can be emitted by the existing backends.

## Acceptance

- Construct a structural representation for object literals when no named target shape exists. Reuse the same synthesized shape for equivalent field layouts, including literals whose property order differs.
- Handle object literals used in assignments, arguments, return values, nested structures, and contextual union or optional types. Empty object literals should use the appropriate contextual shape when one is available.
- Preserve optional and readonly property information. A readonly view must not create an incompatible physical layout for an otherwise equivalent shape.
- Handle record-like object literals without forcing them into an incompatible class shape. Keep existing named-shape behavior and backend output working.
- The resulting HIR must verify and emit through the existing ABAP and Go backends without regressions.

## Notes

Existing behavior must not regress. You may run the project's tests. Work only inside the current repository.
